text:
Maya K: Quick sync — we're starting a controlled deprecation of the legacy precision interop adapter (v1). Goal: remove maintenance burden and unblock the unified profile pipeline. Planning a staged pipeline w/ feature flag, shim, and migration tooling.

Ajay P: +1. rough timeline?

Maya K: Tentative: announce now, enable compatibility shim as default for 6 weeks, then opt-in canary for v2-only endpoints for 4 weeks, then gradual opt-out. Total ~12 weeks but flexible.

Sofia R: Important to surface perf/quality delta per-customer. We should emit a per-request header and aggregate metric so product owners can see regressions fast.

Evan L: Agree. Suggest metrics: precision_profile_used, fallback_reason, delta_token_loss (sampled). Also expose rollup by model+profile.

Liam T: For rollout safety, can we auto-fallback to v1 when degscore crosses threshold? Ops wants automatic rollback for noisy customers.

Maya K: Yes — runtime supports a fallback hook. Plan: canary policy = allow v2; if degscore > 0.08 or latency > 2x baseline on 1% sample, flip to shim for that customer route.

Ajay P: Migration tool idea: `rwd-quant-check --profile v2 --model X --sample N` that runs shadow eval and outputs summary (ppl, auc, sample diffs). Worth building now?

Sofia R: Love it. Make output JSON lines so infra can ingest. e.g.:
```
{"model":"redwood/7b","profile":"v2","ppl_delta":0.03,"fail_rate":0.002}
```
This helps the rollout dashboard.

Evan L: Telemetry detail: include `sample_id` hash, `seed_prompt_bucket`, and an anonymized diff fingerprint (sha1) for drift triage. No raw user content.

Liam T: Ops note: need a flag in Dedicated and Private to disable automatic fallback per-tenant. Enterprise customers may want to manage fallback policies themselves.

Maya K: Good call. We'll add `precision.automated_fallback = true|false` to tenant config. Default true for hosted. Document in release notes.

Ajay P: Interface boundary question — should the shim live in the runtime process or as a sidecar? Sidecar gives us faster iteration but adds network hop. Thoughts?

Sofia R: Sidecar lets us A/B different shims without runtime release. For latency-sensitive paths we should offer an in-process lightweight shim. Hybrid approach?

Maya K: Hybrid sounds right: sidecar for full-featured compatibility, in-process fast-path for hot paths. We'll gate in-process behind `hotpath=true` in the profile.

Evan L: Need a checklist for QA before flipping a customer: 1) shadow-eval passes thresholds, 2) 7-day traffic mirror looks stable, 3) perf benchmarks within 10% CPU/GPU, 4) no new determinism regressions.

Liam T: Ops will own the runbook. Can we add an automated canary job that runs those checks and posts a verdict to #release-war-room?

ops-bot: Scheduled job created: `quant-deprecation-canary/1749995555` will run nightly and post status to #release-war-room.

Sofia R: One more: migration docs should include common gotchas (KV cache layout changes, quant table rounding differences, seed sensitivity). Add a short troubleshooting section with `--replay-seed` and `--force-shim` commands.

Maya K: I'll draft the RFC follow-up doc with the pipeline diagram and checklist. Will ping eng-ml PR when ready. Thanks all — small action items: Ajay to prototype `rwd-quant-check`, Evan to spec telemetry keys, Liam to draft runbook, Sofia to start docs.

Ajay P: I'll put a prototype in a sandbox repo and share a link tomorrow.

Evan L: Telemetry spec by EOD Friday.

Liam T: Runbook draft by next Tue.

Sofia R: Docs skeleton in the docs repo by Monday.

Maya K: Great — keeping the deprecation low-risk. Will post the RFC follow-up and a proposed schedule later today. :thumbsup:
